title: Approving artifact type activation has no typed operation
statement: #39 authorises a state transition — the PM approves an activation list at stage 2, recorded in project.yaml — and nothing can perform it. readActivatedTypes reads it; no typed operation writes it. Should there be one, and what must it validate?
notes: Found by auditing authorised transitions against typed operations (#121's corrected criterion). Every other transition has one: create, link/unlink, revise, setLifecycle, writeStageAttestation, writeReviewStatus, allocateId. This is the only authorised transition still performed by hand-editing a file. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-18: an earlier note said this operation must also move stages/ and #38 with it. That is wrong and crosses the line #95 draws. PROJECT ACTIVATION MUST NOT REWRITE THE CATALOGUE OR THE METHODOLOGY — #107's three-authority update applies when a type is RETIRED FROM THE CATALOGUE, not when a project activates or deactivates an existing one. A project-scoped approval that edited stages/ or #38 would silently become a product-wide design change. The contract is therefore: update the project's approved activation set; record or require the approving decision (#39 makes it agent-proposes/PM-approves, so an activation with no decision behind it is the attestation problem again); and VALIDATE that the type exists in the catalogue and is compatible with the stage definitions. Validate against stages/ and #38 — never write to them. Not blocking under DEC-0002: nothing pending requires an activation change, so it is work rather than a gap.
answer: Implemented as `lib/tools/activate-type.mjs` (`setTypeActivation`), and used to activate `component` rather than hand-editing the manifest. It validates catalogue membership, authorability and stage reachability, writes only the activated list, and refuses to deactivate a type whose artifacts still exist. See DEC-0008.
